summary: Sprint M9 · Venues ownership sync — 2nd bug retest. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_venues_m9_retest.py with 7 new tests covering the model_dump(exclude_unset=True) branches added by main agent (POST both-set-owner-wins, POST neither-set, PATCH only-body_id, PATCH only-owner_body_id, and BCCI calendar-eligible mirror parametrised over Domestic/International/None). All 24 tests pass (100%). Bug is CONFIRMED FIXED.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/venues_grounds.py update_venue accepts full VenueCreate (requires name/category/city). A true PATCH semantic would be more idiomatic via a VenueUpdate model with all-Optional fields — currently the endpoint is more like a full-replace. Not a blocker (tests still assert correct sync), but worth revisiting for next sprint.

_normalise_venue_payload is now partly redundant since the endpoints already force-sync body_id ← owner in the explicit-intent branch. It only helps as a defensive net when both branches fall through (i.e., both defaulted). Consider adding a code comment or unifying the logic to avoid dual sources of truth.
test_credentials: not required — venues endpoints are unauthenticated in this build
seed_data_creation: 8 M9-prefixed venues were created in-flight and all cleaned up by test_zzz_cleanup_m9_venues; verified 0 M9 venues remain post-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_24 confirms M9 owner/body sync bug from iteration_22/23 is fixed. The retest file /app/backend/tests/test_venues_m9_retest.py now covers 24 cases: 4 create-mirror, 3 patch-mirror, 5 seeded regression, 2 filter regression, 2 unknown-body 400, 4 explicit-intent sync (neither/both/patch-body/patch-owner), 3 bcci_calendar mirror, 1 cleanup. Total /api/venues seeded=5 (Holkar, Aishbagh, Jabalpur, Captain Roop Singh, MPCA Indore Academy). Frontend was NOT re-tested per E1 note (passed in iteration_22).
rca of the issue: Fix verified. RCA (already resolved by E1): The old create/update endpoints called _normalise_venue_payload which only filled MISSING keys — so when a client sent owner_body_id='DIV-IND', body_id still carried the Pydantic default 'MPCA' and the normaliser saw body_id as 'set' and refused to overwrite it. E1's fix distinguishes explicitly-set fields via payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) and force-syncs the counterpart: owner-only ⇒ body_id ← owner; body_id-only ⇒ owner ← body_id; both ⇒ owner wins; neither ⇒ both default MPCA. All four branches are now covered by tests.
